en: Catalogue of the Transmission of the Lamp in the Eastern Region, Compiled by the Śramaṇa Eicho of Kōfuku-ji Temple;
Part One: Record of the Propagation of the Sūtras.

The Record of the Transmission of the Vinaya (2), the Record of Lectures and Debates (3), the Record of Miscellaneous Writings (4), and the Record of Biographies (5). In the eighth year of Kōchō, Eishō himself proofread and verified these texts and presented them to Seiren-in at the age of eighty-one. This was because his vow to propagate the Dharma was inexhaustible; such is the full account.
1. Record of the Propagation of the Sūtras (Hongjing lu). Section One: Avataṃsaka Division. *Avataṃsaka-śāstra*, six hundred fascicles.
Compiled by Liu Qianzhi; the characters "Qianzhi" are his name. The "Chuan" refers to the *Huayan chuan* (Avataṃsaka Commentary), five fascicles, compiled by the Master of the Canon (Zangshi).
Also, the *Śāstra* in one hundred fascicles, compiled by the Northern Wei śramaṇa Shi Lingbian. The extant versions are those currently in circulation.

The first fifty fascicles follow the same scriptural model; the *Five Fascicles on the Scriptural Model* (*Fanggui*) was composed by Zhiyan of Zhixiang Monastery on Mount Zhongnan during the Tang dynasty.

He was the first patriarch of the Huayan school. There are also the *Five Fascicles on the Transmission of the Scriptural Model*, the *Four Fascicles on the Miscellaneous Catalogue of the Same Scripture* (the internal title of which reads "The Internal Chapters and Sections of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra," etc.), and the *Question and Answer on the Same Scripture*.

Two fascicles; the same as above. Also, the *Brief Commentary* (*Lüeshu*) [in two fascicles]; the same as above. *The Essential Decisions on the Profound Clarification of the Same Sutra* (*Tongjing xuanying ya jue*), one fascicle;

the same as above. *The Ritual for the Ten Gates of Offering to the Same Sutra* (*Tongjing gongyang shimen yishi*), one fascicle; the same as above. *The Ten Mysterious Chapters on the Same Sutra* (*Tongjing shixuan zhang*), one fascicle, composed by Cheng Dushun.

The above six works were all composed by the same master. *The Record of Investigating the Profundities of the Same Sutra* (*Tongjing tantuan ji*), twenty fascicles, [compiled at] Xichong [Monastery] in Jingzhao.

Compiled by the Śramaṇa Fazang of Fusi Temple. It is also said that the *One Scroll on the Common Return to the Essential Meaning of the Sūtras* by the Śramaṇas of Xisi Temple in the Wei State consists of ten sections, as recorded in the tradition:
first, the place where the sūtra was preached; second, the time when the sūtra was preached; third, the Buddha who preached the sūtra; fourth, the assembly for whom the sūtra was preached;

fifth, the ritual protocol of preaching the sūtra; sixth, the teachings of the sūtra; seventh, the manifestation of the sūtra’s meaning; eighth, the explanation of the sūtra’s intent; ninth, the discernment... [text ends].

*Jingyi shishijingyuan* (The Scripture’s Benefit, Tenfold Exposition, and the Perfection of the Scripture). To the right: based on the ten meanings explained within each of the ten preceding sections, one hundred sections are comprehensively analyzed to reveal the intent of the scripture.
This thereby causes the vast and flowing purport to be gathered before one's eyes. [End of] *Tonggangmu*, one fascicle. Regarding the ten sections and eight assemblies:
the chapters of the *Gangmu* cannot be cited separately; the chapters of the eight assemblies are identical to those in the *Xuanyi* (Profound Meaning) chapter.

One fascicle; *Tongjiaofen ji* (Record of the Shared Teaching Division) in three fascicles—also referred to as the *Yichengjiaofen ji* (Record of the One Vehicle Teaching Division) or the *Wujiaofen ji* (Record of the Five Teachings Division).

These three works, along with those authored by Du Shun, are recorded as having been compiled from outside the major commentaries (*dazhangshu*), recording explanations given according to the questions of others and according to specific meanings, all within the same volumes to clarify the intent of this sutra, and so forth.
*The Single-Scroll Contemplation of the Same Samādhi*, Ten Gates. The preface states: "Regarding the above ten gates, each is also analyzed through ten meanings to clarify what is essential.

This is intended to ensure that one cultivates and perfects the vows and practices of Samantabhadra, binds oneself to the diamond lineage, and establishes the cause for Bodhi, so that in the future one may participate in the ocean-like assembly of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.
Through this, one seeks the methods of the *Tiantai* contemplation of the *Lotus Sūtra* samādhi."

The *Practitioner’s Footprint of Mind and Objects* (in two volumes, including the Question and Answer), the *Comparative Discourse on the Three Teachings* (one volume), the *Chapter on Consciousness-Only* (one volume), the *Ocean of Meaning of the Dharma Realm* (one volume), the *Record of Roaming the Dharma Realm* (one volume), the *Chapter on Arousing the Bodhicitta* (one volume), the *Meaning of the Vital Pulse* (one volume), and the [Treatise on] the Three... [etc.

(Note: The provided text fragment appears to be a bibliographic catalog of several short treatises or chapters attributed to a specific author or school, likely from the Silla or early Goryeo period of Korean Buddhism.)
*Baoli* (Treasure Homage), one fascicle, ten chapters; *Tongzanli* (Homage with Shared Praise), one fascicle, ten chapters; *Jingangshizi Zhang* (Chapter on the Vajra Lion), one fascicle;
*Tongfanji* (Record of Corresponding Translations from Sanskrit), one fascicle; *Gujing tongfanshu yiyi* (Sanskrit Texts and Phonetic Explanations for the Old Scriptures), two fascicles;

*Xinjing xuzhu* (Preface and Commentary to the New Scripture), one fascicle. The above two sections are recorded as having been transmitted. Regarding the Sanskrit terms contained within these new and old scriptures:
The difficult characters in the new scriptures are all provided here with translations and phonetic glosses; these are truly essential for those who read the sutras.

[The following] are recorded together: five volumes of *Biographies*, ten sections on categories, hidden and manifest [teachings], transmission and translation, branches and streams, commentaries and exegeses, lectures and explanations, chanting and recitation, transcription and copying, miscellaneous writings, and the transmission of phonetics and meanings.
Altogether, including the *Tanxuan ji* (Probing the Profundities), these comprise twenty works in total.
Also included is the *Diagram of the Dharma-realm of the One Vehicle* in one fascicle and the *Outline* in one fascicle, both composed by Master Fazang;

the *Commentary on the Same Sutra* in ten fascicles, composed by Master Wonhyo; the *Explanatory Commentary on the Same Sutra* in seven fascicles, composed by Śramaṇa Famin of Jinglin Monastery in Yuezhou during the Tang dynasty;
and the *Explanatory Commentary* in [seven] fascicles, composed by Master Tanzun of Ye in the Qi dynasty. All these are extant.
*Commentary on the Same [Sutra]* in seven fascicles, compiled by Vinaya Master Hongzun of Daxingshan Monastery in the Western Capital during the Sui Dynasty;
*Biography of the Same Commentary* in ten fascicles (traditionally said to be eleven fascicles), compiled by Master Zhizheng of Zhixiang Monastery on Mount Zhongnan during the Tang Dynasty;

*Commentary on the Same [Sutra]* in ten fascicles, compiled by Master Guang of Puguang Monastery in the Capital during the Tang Dynasty; *Commentary on the Same [Sutra]* in seven fascicles, [compiled by] [Master] Jing of the Western Capital during the Sui Dynasty.
The *Tongyi chao* (Excerpts on Identical Meanings) in ten fascicles, composed by Master Huiyuan of Ying Temple, remains unfinished and has not yet been lectured upon.

The *Chuan* (Biography/Record) states that it was composed by the Śramaṇa Lingbian of Da Ci’en Temple in the Tang capital; it says there are twelve fascicles of the *Chu* (Excerpts) and ten fascicles of the *Chao* (Excerpts).

The *Ji* (Record) states that the *Tanxuan ji* says there are ten fascicles composed by the same master, and the three fascicles of the *Huayan zhang* (Chapters on the Avataṃsaka) may be recorded separately.

The *Chuzong mulu* (Catalogue of Excerpts from the Canon) states that there are seven fascicles of the *Tongshu* (Commentary on the Common Text), compiled by the monk Zhiju of Beitaishan during the Wei dynasty; its biography says it consists of ten fascicles.
There are also four fascicles of the *Tongshu*, compiled by the monk Huiguang of Dajuesi in Ye under the Northern Qi dynasty;

its biography says that it was he who first established the three teachings of Gradual, Sudden, and Perfect to classify the various scriptures, taking the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra* as the Perfect Teaching (*yuanjiao*). And so forth. The same.
The *Sūtra Commentary* (Shu) in five fascicles, composed by Śramaṇa Sengfan of Dajue Monastery under Ye in the Qi Dynasty;

the *Biography* states that he also produced commentaries on the *Vimalakīrti*, *Śrīmālā*, *Daśabhūmika*, and *Bhūmisaṃgraha*, etc. The *Same Commentary* (Tongshu) in seven fascicles, composed by Śramaṇa Tanyan of Zhaozhou in the Qi Dynasty.

The *Same Meaning Commentary* (Tongyishu) in ten fascicles, composed by Śramaṇa Huizang of Kongguan Monastery in the Western Capital during the Sui Dynasty; the *Biography* states that he also produced the same commentary.

The eight-fascicle *Chuan* (Biographies/Records), compiled by Shi Lingyou of Yan’kong Monastery in Xiangzhou during the Sui dynasty, states that he also produced various other commentaries (*zhanshu*), records (*chuanyi*), and so forth, totaling over one hundred fascicles.
It further records instances where he perceived empty sounds and auspicious omens, and so on.

The *Tongzhigui* (Unifying the Essential Return) in one fascicle and its commentary in ten fascicles were both compiled by Shi Huijue of Wude Monastery in Bingzhou during the Tang dynasty; these constitute the *Huayan jing hui shi* (Exegesis of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra).
The *Treatise* (Lun) in fourteen fascicles; the *Commentary on the New Sutra* (Xin jing tong jing shu) by Li Tongxuan in thirty fascicles, titled *Yanyi*;

and the *Commentary on the New Sutra* (Xin jing qingliang shan da hua yan si banruo yuan chengguan shi zhu) composed by Master Chengguan of the Prajñā Hall at the Great Huayan Monastery on Mount Qingliang.

These are divided into primary and secondary sections, totaling sixty fascicles. When the two sets of eighty-four [fascicles] are combined, they comprise seventy fascicles. The commentaries on the eighty sutras are likewise divided into primary and secondary sections.
The *Commentary on the Thirty Sūtras* in sixty fascicles; furthermore, there are ten fascicles [of other works], and so forth.
The *Commentary on the Samantabhadra-caryā-praṇidhāna* in one fascicle, same as above. The *Mysterious Mirror of the Dharma-realm Contemplation* on the same sūtra in ten fascicles, same as above.
The *Record for Determining the Text* in sixteen fascicles, composed by Master Huìyuǎn of Jìngqīng Monastery in Jīngzhào. The *Chapter on the Revolving Repentance* in ten fascicles, same as above.

*Shangxuanfu xuanyu tong yinyi* (The Combined Phonology and Meaning of the *Shangxuanfu Xuanyu*), two fascicles; same as above. *Xinjing dacheng quan shi yi* (The Meaning of the Provisional and Real in the New Sūtra of the Mahāyāna), two fascicles;
same as above. *Same Sūtra Commentary* (*Tong jing shu*), twenty fascicles; composed by Master Zongyi of the new sūtra. *Same Sūtra Commentary*, thirteen fascicles; same commentary.
*Same Commentary on the "Chapter on Difficulties"* (*Nan pin shu*), ten fascicles; [composed by] Dao[sheng] of Xijing Chanding Monastery during the Sui dynasty.
Compiled by Tánqiān of the Zhǎngchăng [monastery]. Also compiled is the *Dàchéng zhǐguān* (One Scroll);

I privately note that some title it as compiled by the Great Master of Nányuè, yet its text and meaning are entirely identical. The *Tóng rùfǎjiè pǐn chāo* (One Scroll) was compiled by Guāngtǒng Lǜshī.
The *Tóng yóuyì* (One Scroll) was compiled by Master Jízàng; it appears in the catalog of the Sanlùn school. The *Tóng gùmù* (One Scroll) is new.
*Jingzhānshī zhuàn chū Tiāntái zōnglù tóng jīng zhǐguī* (The Record of the Tiantai School Compiled by Master Jingzhān, with the Return to the Intent of the Same Sutra), two fascicles;
compiled by the Śramaṇa Fáyè of Nánlín during the Eastern Jin. *Tóng jīng wǔjiào fēnjì* (A Record of the Five Teachings of the Same Sutra), one fascicle; compiled by Master Dúshùn.

*Tóng fǎjiè guān* (Contemplation of the Same Dharmadhātu), one fascicle; same as above. *Wánzhēnrén lù shàn Cái tóngzi zhū zhīshí lù* (Record of the Good and Wise Friends of the Youth Sudhana), compiled by Shì Yànzōng.
The *Compilation of the Names of Bodhisattvas from the Same Sūtras* in three fascicles is divided into two parts:
the *Names of Buddhas* in two fascicles and the *Names of Bodhisattvas* in one fascicle. According to tradition, it is unknown who compiled these;

they were gathered from various sources and were incomplete, so the śramaṇa Xianshou further expanded upon the original material, making it quite detailed. [There is also] the *Method for Universal Prostration* in one fascicle.
The *Fifteen Prostrations* (Wǔshí bǎi) is said to have been compiled by the Meditation Master Zhìyǐ of Mount Tiantāi.

Its prostrations all refer to "universal worship" (*pǔlǐ*), rather than specifically addressing Vairocana Buddha. Within the text, the names of the seven locations and eight assemblies—such as the site of the Great Parinirvāṇa—are listed in detail.

This work is currently widely practiced in the region south of the Yangtze River; thus, I shall not provide an exhaustive commentary here. Furthermore, Zhìyǐ classified the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* as belonging to the Perfect Teaching (*yuán*).

*Man-dun yun-yun t'ung-kyǒng ch'i-chi* (Complete Record of the Simultaneous Sutra), one fascicle; compiled by Prince Wenxuan of Jingling. *T'ung-wen-i ryak-tsuan* (Brief Compendium of the Shared Textual Meaning), one fascicle.

*T'ung-kyǒng hoe-sin-i* (Meaning of the Conversion of Mind through the Shared Sutra), one fascicle. *T'ung-kyǒng sip-hoe* (The Ten Assemblies of the Shared Sutra), one fascicle. *T'ung-kyǒng pin-hoe-myǒng tu* (Diagram of the Names and Assemblies of the Shared Sutra), one fascicle.

*T'ung-ch'ǒng hyǒn-seǒng-mun* (Text for Invoking the Worthies and Sages), one fascicle. *T'ung-kyǒng nyǒn-hwa-jang se-je-kwan* (Contemplation of the Lotus Treasury World-Ocean according to the Shared Sutra).
*The Visualization of Maitreya’s Heavenly Palace*, one fascicle; compiled by Linggan of Dajian Ding Temple in the Western Capital during the Sui dynasty.
*The Treatise on the Sea-Seal Samādhi*, one fascicle; compiled by Master Minghao. *The Record of the Essential Points of the Flower Garland [Sūtra]*, six fascicles;

compiled by Master Zhensong of Silla. *The Concordant Record of the Essential Points*, two fascicles. *Pointing to the Facts of the Five Teachings*, three fascicles; [compiled by] Shou [of] Xingfu Temple.

*Wajō Go-kyō Shiki* (Private Record of the Five Teachings in Japanese), two fascicles, compiled by the śramaṇa Gwan’en. *Tōkyō Gen-gen Kan* (Contemplation on Returning to the Source of the Same Sūtra), one fascicle;
recorded in the *Shinkōroku*. *Tōkyō Shiki* (Private Record of the Same Sūtra), two fascicles, [compiled by] Ushin.

*Tōkyō Ju Bodai-shin Kai* (Receiving the Bodhicitta Precepts of the Same Sūtra), one fascicle, [compiled by] Ushin. *Tōkyō Ryōkenshō* (Examination of the Same Sūtra), one fascicle; recorded in the *Zentō-in*.

*Lu hui zhong tong jing lüe shu* (Record of the Explanations on the Compendium of the Sūtras by Huizhong), six fascicles; the six fascicles of various sūtra catalogs may be found within the table of contents of this *shu*.

*Tong jing lüe shu zhi shi* (Explanatory Matters on the Compendium of the Sūtras), eight fascicles; *Tong jing yao ji liao jian* (Essential Collection and Analysis of the Compendium of the Sūtras), one fascicle; both are as above. *Tong lüe shu zhi shi* (Explanatory Matters on the Compendium of the Sūtras), one fascicle;
*Xin jing tong yi cheng fa jie tu* (Diagram of the Dharma Realm of the One Vehicle according to the New Sūtras), one fascicle; by Fazang.

The *Zuǎn kě rù shàng èrshí bù děng* (Compendium of the Twenty Superior Sections, etc.), which the Southern Capital edition notes as being personally stated to have been compiled by the Tang monk Yixiang;
he is titled Venerable Fushí and was a native of Silla. The twentieth volume of the *Yuánzōng wénlèi* contains the letter from Fazang to Yixiang.

Also included is one scroll of the *Shàngtóng qīchù jiūhuì sòng* (Verses on the Seven Locations and Nine Assemblies) and the same volume contains the commentary on the preface to the aforementioned sutra.

One scroll of the *Shanryōjutsu* (Excellently Stated Account of the Scroll), with the same preface as above, recorded privately; one scroll of the *Muso-zenshi Aba-chōshin Jinjō-shū* (Collection of the Late Minister of the Left, Aba Chōshin, of the Muzo Clan).
The items from *Gendan-kan* (Observations on Returning to the Source) onwards are not included in the records of that school and must be verified later.

The *Huayan suishu yanyi chao* (Commentary on the Explication of the Meaning of the Avataṃsaka Commentary) consists of thirty fascicles; among these, Master Guan’s *Zhenlu* (Precious Record) first cites twenty fascicles of the commentary and presents them separately, which may be examined in detail.
If the preceding and succeeding portions were combined, would there not have been sixty fascicles? Because the root and the branches were divided, it likely reached eighty.
Recently, according to the tradition of the Huayan school at Tōdai-ji, it is said that Master Guan first produced the version for the new translation of the sutra.

The *Shu* (Commentary) in ten fascicles was followed by the *Suishu Yanyi Chao* (Sub-commentary Expounding the Meaning of the Commentary) in twenty fascicles; each was divided into root and commentary, totaling sixty fascicles.
Later, he composed the *Sishijingshu* (Commentaries on Forty Sutras) in ten fascicles, bringing the total to seventy fascicles of textual commentaries, and so forth. Also included are:

one fascicle on the shared reception of the Bodhicitta precepts, and four fascicles of the Master Tiantai Guanding’s *Renwang Jing Shu* (Commentary on the Benevolent Kings Sutra), transcribed by Lunfa.

The inscription for the Master is recorded in the *Yuanzong lu* (Record of the Perfect School). According to the original record, one fascicle of the *Preface* and three fascicles of the *Commentary* were included, while the *Private Notes* (*Siji*) were not.
Now, according to my private examination, the *Commentary* and *Private Notes* together may constitute four fascicles;

this is seen from the inscription, which states that the *Jin Guangming Xuan* (Profound Meaning of the Golden Light) and the *Wenju* (Words and Phrases) both consist of four fascicles of commentary, and this case is likewise so.

The differences in their rankings are not uniform and cannot be fixed; later scholars have fully understood this. Jizang’s commentary and the *Huguo chao* (Notes by Huguoku) cite it, from which one may further grasp its intent.
There is one work in two fascicles titled *Shizhu jing shu* (Commentary on the Ten Stages Sutra), whose author is unknown.

Regarding the *Huayan fangdeng* (Avataṃsaka Vaipulya) and the *Keding banruo bu* (Determined Prajñā Section), there is one fascicle titled *Banguo jing ji* (Record of the Pañcaviṃśati-sāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra), which appears in the ancient catalogs of Dao [Xuan].

*Fangdeng xingjing houji* (Postscript to the *Pratyutpanna-samādhi Sūtra*), one fascicle; *Dapin banruo jing zhu* (Commentary on the *Pañcaviṃśati-sāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*), fifty fascicles, compiled by Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty together with Fachong of Tianbao Temple.
The *Sanlun lu* states that these were annotated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva and others; if they were separate commentaries, [this would be the case].

*Dapin banruo jing lue shu* (Abbreviated Commentary on the *Pañcaviṃśati-sāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*), four fascicles, composed by Jizang. *Dapin banruo jing guang shu* (Extensive Commentary on the *Pañcaviṃśati-sāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*), ten fascicles, same author as above. Six copies from the Nanto edition.
The *Commentary on the Scroll* (one scroll), visible at Tōji; the *Intent of the Shared Study* (one scroll, same as above); or the *Six-Scroll Commentary*;
Master Jizang’s *Commentary* (one scroll, Tōji original copy); the *Shared Commentary* (five scrolls, compiled by Dharma Master Lin); the *Shared Sectional Text* (one scroll, twenty-four sheets);
and the *Profound Meaning of the Sutra* (four scrolls, compiled by Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha). These constitute the *Commentary on the Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.

One fascicle, a commentary on the same sutra composed by Master Huiyuan; one fascicle, a commentary on the same sutra composed by Chan Master Tiantai Zhiyi—both of which I perused in previous years and found to be similar to the commentary by Sengzhao;

unexpectedly, there are also four fascicles of a commentary on the same sutra composed by Jizang, four fascicles of a commentary on the same sutra composed by Huixian, and two fascicles of a commentary on the same sutra composed by Han Guang, continuing down to the commentaries by Jingmai. The Dharma... [is thus preserved].

The *Xiangzong tonglue ji* (Abridged Record on the Commonality of the Dharma-character School) in one fascicle; the same author’s *Tongshu* (Commentary on the Commonality) in two fascicles, which states that the *Shuzan* (Eulogy and Commentary) was composed by Da Ci’en Si Master Dasheng Ji;

the *Tongxuan ji* (Record on the Profound Meaning of the Commonality) in ten fascicles; and the *Shanzhu Weishi ganxin ji* (Record on the Vital Essence of Consciousness-Only by Shanzhu), which states:
"The *Xuanji* (Profound Record) refers to the commentary on Asaṅga’s *Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra* as expounded by Master Ji; this is what circulates in the world today."
[The text] states: "Please consult the *Yunyun qin* (云云親); [the text] states: 'The *Tonghui shi* (同會釋) in three fascicles, as mentioned above;

the *Wujing erlun huishi* (五經二論會釋) and the *Tongsu* (同疏) in two fascicles, compiled by Jingmai of the New Translation School. The *Dongsi lu* (東寺錄) records: 'The *Nenduan jing shu* (能斷經疏) in one fascicle.
It can be seen that this corresponds to the *Tongsu* in two fascicles compiled by Wŏnhyo; the *Seodan lu* (西端錄) records it as being divided into two fascicles."

The *Commentary on the Same Sutra* (Dōkyōsho) in four fascicles was produced by Eshin Chisha (Ennin); its transmission is recorded in the *Soshōsho*. It states, "As in the *Hannya Dōsho*," and so forth.
The *Commentary on the Same Sutra* in three fascicles is recorded in the *Daigun Enkei Shinroku* and the *Denpō-inroku*.

The *Komonbun of the Same Sutra* in one fascicle—there is doubt as to whether the temple name "Daigun" was composed by Enkei. The *Sen'en of the Same Sutra* in three fascicles is said to have been produced [by imperial command].
*Commentary on the Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*: Expounded by Xuanyan, with the *Eulogy on the Initial Preface* (*Suihe zantan lun*) composed by the Śramaṇa Daoyin of Qinglong Monastery;

the *Explanatory Notes on the Same Sūtra* (*Tongjing jue*) in one fascicle; the *Hymn to the Same Sūtra* (*Tongjing tan*) as titled at Caoxi in three fascicles; the *Brief Record of the Same [Sūtra]* (*Tonglue ji*) in one fascicle composed by Dundun;

the *Profound Meaning of the Same Sūtra* (*Tongjing xuanyi*) in one fascicle; and the *Commentary on the Same Sūtra* (*Tongjing shu*) in two fascicles, also known as the *Condensed Version* (*Shanben*).
*Supplementary Commentary on the Meaning of the Same Sutra*, one fascicle, composed by Shen Ying of Ximing Monastery;

*Annotated Commentary on the Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle, attributed to the Oxhead School; *Commentary on the Same Collection*, one fascicle, composed by the Yao Qin śramaṇa Shi Sengzhao;
*Preface to the Commentary*, one sheet, composed by Shanggong Yi; *Commentary on the Same*, one fascicle, [composed by] He, Court Doctor of the Grand Ministry.
One fascicle of the *Commentary on the Same* compiled by Nanyue Liang; one fascicle of the *Commentary on the Same* compiled by Master Rong of Niutou Mountain in Jiangning.
Regarding the *Mahā-śāstra-vyākhyāna* by Vajragarbha Bodhisattva, some editions include it among the spurious translations, while others state that King Sanchuan judged it to be apocryphal.
Having now examined it closely, I find it truly difficult to [dismiss].

*Shintō-chū* (Commentary on Concordance), three fascicles; *Nangaku Wajaku Dōchū* (Concordant Commentary by Nanyue Wang Jie), one fascicle; *Gochū Dōzoku Ki* (Imperial Commentary and Records of Monastics and Laity), three fascicles.

These were the words of the Master of Men who recorded the transmission of the *Kishin-ki* (Record of the Transmission of the Awakening of Faith); they were used for the purpose of proclaiming and expounding [the teaching].
The ancient masters all utilized the *Kongōsenron* (Vajrasamādhi-śāstra), ten fascicles, translated by Bodhiruci and composed by Vajrasena—said to be a disciple of Vasubandhu, and so forth.

*Same Root Record* (Dongben ji), four fascicles; translated by Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha; its original manuscript has not been seen. Is it perhaps similar to the *Mahāyāna-śāstra*, which was not used in earlier generations, or is it distinct from others?
*Commentary on the Same Sūtra* (Tong jing shu), one fascicle. The *Original Text of the Practice of Great Compassion* (Beici jianxing ben) states:
"The record consists of forty-two sheets, compiled by the śramaṇa Beici to instruct the ignorant," and so forth. There are verses interspersed within it; these are likely additions.
The Great Being (Mahāsattva) composed [the commentary]... this sub-commentary was authored by Upādhyāya Pao-chih... *Tong-jian Jing-ji* (Record of Experiences of the Same Sūtra), three fascicles;
*Si-ji* (Private Record), one fascicle; *Tong-jian Jing-ji Xin* (New Record of Experiences of the Same Sūtra), one fascicle;

*Giketsu keshutsu setsuki* (Notes on the Sectional Exegesis of the Decisions on Meaning) in four fascicles; *Dō* (Discourse) in five fascicles; *Saishō no shosha keshutsu setsuki* (Notes on the Sectional Exegesis of the Commentary by Saishō-no-sho) in six fascicles; and the *Nehan gyō* (Nirvāṇa Sūtra) in forty fascicles.

*Wenda yiyin yi* (Meanings of Questions and Answers), one fascicle; *Zhishi* (Pointing to Matters), one fascicle; *Huayan Shizhu yi* (Meanings of the Ten Abodes of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra), one fascicle; *Wenda* (Questions and Answers), one fascicle; *Lüchao* (Brief Abstract), one fascicle;

*Sanjiao ji* (Record of the Three Teachings), one fascicle; *Shilun jing lüchao* (Brief Abstract of the Daśacakrakṣitigarbha-sūtra), one fascicle; *Bore xinjing youzan jiejie ji shilun zhu* (Commentary on the Profound Praise of the Heart Sūtra: Record of Sectional Explanations and Notes on the Śāstra), two fascicles; *Ershiwenshilun lüchao* (Brief Abstract of the Viṃśatikā-vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra), one fascicle;

*Sanshewenshilun lüeshi* (Brief Explanation of the Triṃśikā-vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra), one fascicle; *Shu jiejie ji* (Record of Sectional Explanations of the Commentary), twenty fascicles; *Shuyao jiejie ji* (Record of Sectional Explanations of the Pivotial Essentials), seventeen fascicles; *Fayuan linzhang* (Forest Chapters from the Garden of the Dharma).

*Jiejue ji* (Record of the Explanation of the *Vibhāṣā*) in twenty fascicles; *Inming shu jiejue ji* (Commentary on the *Hetuvidyā* with Record of the Explanation of the *Vibhāṣā*) in twenty fascicles—those listed above were composed prior to his eightieth year; those written after his eightieth year may be verified [in the following].

*Liaoyi deng jiejue ji* (Lamp of the Definitive Meaning with Record of the Explanation of the *Vibhāṣā*) in three fascicles; *Ming jin'gang banruo jiejue ji* (Record of the Explanation of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*) in three fascicles—these were composed between the ages of eighty-five and ninety based on his own interpretation of the sūtra text, not yet relying on the meaning of the commentaries, and are somewhat sparse and brief.
*Pusa zang apitan guji he* (Combined Ancient Records of the *Bodhisattvapiṭaka-abhidharma*) in seventeen fascicles, compiled by the Śramaṇa Taehyeon of Qingqiu.
The *Śata-dharma-śāstra* consists of seventeen fascicles;
it is not the case that there was an ancient record consisting of one fascicle for each individual dharma.
Therefore, it is said to consist of seventeen fascicles;
its essential meaning is found in the separate record (*bielu*).

The *Mūlamātṛkā-gāthā* in one hundred lines, together with its commentary in three fascicles, is titled the *Xinshu Zhang*. This concludes the *Dongyu Chuandeng Lu* (Record of the Transmission of the Lamp in the Eastern Region).
